en: eliminate (someone from a competition); knock out

examples.ko: 심사위원이 첫 라운드에서 세 팀을 탈락시켰어요.
examples.en: The judges eliminated three teams in the first round.
The company did not eliminate any applicants at the interview.

examples.ko: 실수 하나 때문에 저를 탈락시키다니 너무해요.
examples.en: Eliminating me over a single mistake is too harsh.

examples.ko: 감독이 선수 두 명을 대표팀에서 탈락시킬 거예요.
examples.en: The coach is going to cut two players from the national team.

examples.ko: 약한 팀을 탈락시키고 다음 경기를 시작했어요.
examples.en: They knocked out the weaker teams and started the next match.
Audition programs that eliminate people are nerve-racking.

explain: '떨어지다'는 시험이나 경쟁에서 내가 떨어질 때, '탈락시키다'는 심사하는 쪽이 다른 사람을 떨어뜨릴 때 써요. 당하는 사람 쪽에서는 '탈락하다', '탈락되다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: '떨어지다' is what you say when you fail a test or competition yourself; '탈락시키다' is used by the side doing the judging, who knocks someone out. From the point of view of the person eliminated, you say '탈락하다' or '탈락되다'.

examples.ko: 사람들 앞에서 친구를 모욕하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not humiliate a friend in front of other people.
That customer insulted the staff member.

examples.ko: 외모로 사람을 모욕하는 말은 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Do not say things that insult people for their looks.
I reported the person who insulted me in the comments.
I had no intention of insulting anyone.
After insulting his teacher, he regretted it.

explain: '놀리다'는 장난으로도 쓰지만 '모욕하다'는 상대의 자존심을 심하게 상하게 한다는 느낌이라 훨씬 무거워요. 법에서는 '모욕죄'라고 하고, 일상에서 가볍게 무시할 때는 '무시하다'를 써요.
explain_en: '놀리다' can be playful, but '모욕하다' is much heavier: it means seriously wounding someone's pride. The law has a crime called '모욕죄', and for casually looking down on someone you would use '무시하다'.

en: be concluded; be achieved (a deal, a meeting)

examples.en: After long negotiations, the contract was finalized.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 합병이 곧 성사될 거예요.
examples.en: The merger of the two companies will go through soon.
It was a pity that the appointment didn't work out.

examples.ko: 이번 달에 성사된 거래는 세 건이에요.
examples.en: Three deals were closed this month.
If the talks take place, it will be in the news.
The blind date was arranged, so the two of them met.

explain: 계약, 거래, 회담, 만남처럼 상대가 있는 일이 이루어질 때 써요. 사람이 주어인 '성공하다'와 달리 일이 주어예요. '이루어지다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스와 회사에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is used when something that involves another party, such as a contract, a deal, talks, or a meeting, actually comes together. Unlike '성공하다', which takes a person as subject, the subject here is the matter itself. It sounds stiffer than '이루어지다', so you hear it in the news and at work.

examples.en: The sales team closed a big contract.
I will arrange a meeting between the two of you.
To get the negotiation done, both sides have to compromise.

examples.ko: 그는 어려운 거래를 성사시키는 능력이 있어요.
examples.en: He has the ability to close difficult deals.

examples.ko: 대표님이 직접 나서서 투자를 성사시키고 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: The CEO stepped in personally, secured the investment, and came back.
The person who made the agreement happen is the department head.

explain: '성사되다'는 일이 저절로 이루어진다는 느낌이고, '성사시키다'는 사람이 애써서 이루어 낸다는 느낌이에요. 영업이나 협상 이야기에서 '계약을 성사시키다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: '성사되다' feels like something coming together on its own, while '성사시키다' feels like a person working hard to make it happen. In sales and negotiation talk, '계약을 성사시키다' (to close a contract) is a common phrase.

en: flow in; be introduced from outside

examples.en: The river water flows into the sea.
Foreign culture came in quickly.
The population moving into the city is growing.

examples.ko: 나쁜 정보가 유입되지 않도록 막아야 해요.
examples.en: We have to block bad information from getting in.

examples.ko: 새로운 자금이 유입되면 회사가 살아날 거예요.
examples.en: If new funds flow in, the company will recover.
The water that got in filled the basement.

explain: 물, 사람, 돈, 문화, 정보처럼 바깥에서 안으로 흘러 들어올 때 써요. 반대말은 '유출되다'예요. 일상에서는 '들어오다'를 쓰고, 뉴스나 통계에서 '유입'과 '유출'을 짝으로 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when water, people, money, culture, or information flows from outside to inside. The opposite is '유출되다'. In daily speech people say '들어오다' instead, while in news and statistics you see '유입' and '유출' as a pair.

examples.en: The old warehouse was converted into a cafe.

examples.ko: 이 버스는 이동 도서관으로 개조될 거예요.
examples.en: This bus will be converted into a mobile library.

examples.ko: 개조된 차는 휠체어를 탄 사람도 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: The modified car can be used by people in wheelchairs too.
The area was noisy while the building was being remodeled.

examples.ko: 집이 개조되고 나니 훨씬 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: Now that the house has been remodeled, it looks much bigger.

examples.ko: 옛 공장이 전시장으로 개조되어서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: The old factory was turned into an exhibition hall, so it is popular.

explain: 건물, 차, 기계의 구조나 쓰임을 바꿀 때 써요. 집이나 가게를 새로 꾸밀 때는 '리모델링', 작게 손볼 때는 '고치다'를 많이 말해요. 능동형은 '개조하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when the structure or purpose of a building, vehicle, or machine is changed. For redoing a home or shop, people often say '리모델링', and for small repairs, '고치다'. The active form is '개조하다'.

examples.en: A month has already passed since the contract date.
Throw away milk that is past its expiry date.
Once the set time has elapsed, the door locks automatically.

examples.ko: 신청 기간이 경과되어서 접수할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The application period has passed, so we cannot accept it.

examples.ko: 사고 후 두 시간이 경과되었지만 연락이 없어요.
examples.en: Two hours have passed since the accident, but there is no word.

examples.ko: 일주일이 경과될 때까지 답이 없으면 전화하세요.
examples.en: If there is no answer by the time a week has passed, call us.

explain: 시간이 지났다는 뜻이지만 공문, 안내문, 뉴스에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 대화에서는 '지나다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '시간이 경과하다'처럼 '하다' 형도 써요.
explain_en: It means time has passed, but it is a stiff word used in official notices, announcements, and the news. In conversation '지나다' sounds much more natural. The '하다' form, as in '시간이 경과하다', is used too.

en: give relief to; rescue and aid

examples.en: The firefighters gave aid to the injured people.

examples.ko: 재난 지역의 주민들을 구호하는 단체에 기부했어요.
examples.en: I donated to an organization that gives relief to residents of disaster areas.

examples.ko: 먼저 부상자를 구호하고 나서 병원으로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: They first gave aid to the wounded and then moved them to the hospital.
There are not enough supplies to provide relief to the flood victims.

examples.ko: 적십자는 전쟁 난민을 구호하려고 현장에 갔어요.
examples.en: The Red Cross went to the site to help war refugees.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에서 다친 아이를 구호해 준 분이 있어요.
examples.en: Someone helped the injured child at the scene of the accident.

explain: '돕다'보다 훨씬 무겁고, 재난, 전쟁, 사고처럼 위험한 상황에서 사람을 구하고 돌볼 때만 써요. '구호 물품', '구호 단체'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요. 슬로건 뜻의 '구호'는 한자가 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is far heavier than '돕다' and is only used for rescuing and caring for people in dangerous situations such as disasters, wars, and accidents. It also appears as a noun in '구호 물품' (relief supplies) and '구호 단체' (relief organization). The '구호' meaning slogan is a different word with different Chinese characters.

en: reside permanently; be stationed on site

examples.en: A doctor is on duty at this hospital around the clock.
A manager is stationed in the building, so I feel safe.
The research team is made up of people who live permanently at the Antarctic base.
A building with no guard on site feels unsafe.

examples.ko: 공사 기간에 직원 두 명이 현장에 상주했어요.
examples.en: Two staff members stayed on the site during construction.

examples.ko: 도우미가 상주할 수 있는 방이 필요해요.
examples.en: I need a room where a helper can live.

explain: '살다'는 집이 있는 사람에게 쓰고, '상주하다'는 일하는 사람이 어떤 곳에 계속 머물러 있다는 뜻으로 써요. 안내문에 '직원 상주'라고 많이 보여요. 장례식의 '상주'(주 되는 가족)와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: '살다' is for where a person lives, while '상주하다' means a person who works there stays on site all the time. Signs often say '직원 상주' (staff on site). It is a different word from '상주', the chief mourner at a funeral.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 골대 앞에서 열심히 수비했어요.
examples.en: Our team defended hard in front of the goal.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 상대 에이스를 수비하는 역할이에요.
examples.en: That player's role is to defend against the opposing ace.

examples.ko: 공격할 때보다 수비할 때가 더 힘들어요.
examples.en: Defending is harder than attacking.

examples.ko: 끝까지 수비하고 나서 마지막에 점수를 냈어요.
examples.en: They held the defense until the end and then scored late.
This time they pulled back in order to defend.
We talked with the coach about how we should defend.

explain: 경기에서 점수를 막는 일은 '수비', 점수를 내는 일은 '공격'이에요. 경기 밖에서 물건이나 사람을 지킬 때는 '지키다'를 써요.
explain_en: In a game, stopping the other side from scoring is '수비' and scoring is '공격'. Outside of sports, when you protect an object or a person, use '지키다'.

en: fly or sail on a route; operate (flights, ships)

examples.en: This ship runs to Jeju Island every day.

examples.ko: 비행기가 안개 때문에 운항할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The plane could not fly because of the fog.
Passenger ferries do not operate when a typhoon comes.

examples.ko: 이 항공사는 새벽에도 운항하는 노선이 있어요.
examples.en: This airline has routes that operate even at dawn.
The captain sailed ships for thirty years.

examples.ko: 지금은 하루에 세 번 운항하고 있어요.
examples.en: It currently makes three runs a day.

explain: 비행기와 배가 정해진 길로 다닌다는 뜻이에요. 버스와 지하철은 '운행하다'라고 해서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 하늘과 바다는 '운항', 땅 위는 '운행'이에요.
explain_en: It means planes and ships travel along a set route. Buses and subways use '운행하다', which is easy to mix up: '운항' is for sky and sea, '운행' is for land.

examples.ko: 저는 이 회사에 십 년째 재직하고 있어요.
examples.en: I have been employed at this company for ten years.
He is a teacher who once worked at our school.
I learned a lot while I was employed there.

examples.ko: 재직할 때 만난 사람들과 아직 연락해요.
examples.en: I still keep in touch with the people I met while working there.
Before joining the university, I worked at a research institute.
Working here, I met good people.

explain: 어떤 직장에 속해서 일하고 있을 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. '일하다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 '재직하다'는 서류나 소개에서 '재직 증명서', '재직 중'처럼 써요. 직장을 그만두면 '퇴직하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for being employed by an organization. '일하다' works everywhere, but '재직하다' appears in documents and introductions, as in '재직 증명서' (employment certificate) and '재직 중' (currently employed). When you leave the job, it becomes '퇴직하다'.

examples.en: This machine is very precise.

examples.ko: 정밀한 검사를 받으려면 큰 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: To get a detailed examination, you have to go to a large hospital.
The map is so detailed that even small alleys appear.
The parts inside the watch are made with precision.
If the result is not precise, I will measure again.
The more precise it is, the more expensive it tends to be.

explain: '정확하다'는 틀리지 않았다는 뜻이고, '정밀하다'는 아주 작은 부분까지 꼼꼼하고 세밀하다는 느낌이에요. 기계, 검사, 측정에 잘 어울려요. 사람의 성격을 말할 때는 '꼼꼼하다'를 써요.
explain_en: '정확하다' means free of mistakes, while '정밀하다' feels like careful, fine detail down to the smallest parts. It suits machines, tests, and measurements. For a person's character, use '꼼꼼하다' instead.

examples.en: The negotiations are moving forward little by little.
I am worried because things are not moving ahead quickly.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 진전되면 무역도 늘 거예요.
examples.en: If relations between the two countries advance, trade will grow too.
I will announce the results after the investigation has progressed.

examples.ko: 수사가 진전되어서 범인이 곧 잡힐 것 같아요.
examples.en: The investigation has advanced, so the culprit will probably be caught soon.
Every time the discussion progressed, the mood got better.

explain: 협상, 수사, 관계처럼 일이 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. 일이 주어예요. 사람이 나아질 때는 '발전하다', '나아지다'가 자연스러워요. '진전이 있다', '진전이 없다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a matter such as negotiations, an investigation, or a relationship moves forward, so the subject is the matter itself. When a person improves, '발전하다' or '나아지다' sounds more natural. People also often say '진전이 있다' or '진전이 없다' (there is or is no progress).

examples.en: He was deported for staying illegally.

examples.ko: 그 나라에서 추방된 사람들이 이웃 나라로 갔어요.
examples.en: The people expelled from that country went to a neighboring country.
When the deportation order came down, the family cried.

examples.ko: 학교에서 추방당할 정도로 큰 잘못은 아니에요.
examples.en: It is not a mistake big enough to get you kicked out of school.
That country announced the expulsion of the diplomat.

examples.ko: 왕은 반대하는 신하들을 먼 섬으로 추방했어요.
examples.en: The king banished the officials who opposed him to a distant island.

explain: 나라나 단체에서 사람을 강제로 내보낸다는 느낌이라 뉴스와 역사 이야기에서 나와요. '쫓아내다'는 일상에서 쓰는 말이고, '추방'은 법이나 권력이 내리는 결정에 어울려요. '추방하다', '추방당하다', '추방되다'도 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of forcing someone out of a country or group, so it appears in the news and in history stories. '쫓아내다' is the everyday word, while '추방' suits decisions made by law or those in power. The verb forms '추방하다', '추방당하다', and '추방되다' are also used.

en: be dispatched; go into action (police, fire, rescue)

examples.en: The police were dispatched right after getting the report.

examples.ko: 소방차가 불이 난 곳으로 출동하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear fire engines heading out to the fire.
The paramedics rushed out and took the patient to the hospital.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 제설 차량이 출동할 예정이에요.
examples.en: Since it snowed a lot, snow-removal vehicles are due to go out.

examples.ko: 출동하고 십 분 만에 현장에 도착했어요.
examples.en: They arrived at the scene ten minutes after setting out.

examples.ko: 차가 고장 나면 직원이 바로 출동하나요?
examples.en: If my car breaks down, does a staff member come out right away?

explain: 경찰, 소방, 구급처럼 급한 일을 해결하는 사람들이 현장으로 나갈 때 써요. 일상에서 '가다'로 말하는 자리에 쓰면 어색해요. 농담으로 '친구들 출동!'처럼 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when police, firefighters, or paramedics head out to the scene of an emergency. Using it where you would normally say '가다' sounds odd, though people joke with phrases like '친구들 출동!' (friends, move out!).

examples.en: Metal was detected at the airport security check.
A strange signal was picked up on the radar.
When smoke is detected, an alarm sounds.
The rescue team set out for the detected location.
I was relieved because no virus was detected.

examples.ko: 소리가 너무 작아 탐지될 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The sound was too faint to be detected.

explain: 숨어 있거나 잘 안 보이는 것을 기계나 장치가 찾아낼 때 써요. 사람이 눈으로 찾을 때는 '발견되다'가 자연스러워요. 능동은 '탐지하다'이고, '탐지기', '탐지견'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a machine or device finds something hidden or hard to see. When a person finds something by eye, '발견되다' sounds more natural. The active form is '탐지하다', and it also joins other words, as in '탐지기' (detector) and '탐지견' (detection dog).

en: be opened up; be reclaimed (land); be pioneered

examples.en: New markets are being opened up one by one.
The wasteland was reclaimed as farmland.
It is easy if you follow the path that has been cleared.

examples.ko: 우주가 개척되면 우리도 살 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Once space is opened up, could we live there too?

examples.ko: 이 땅은 백 년 전에 개척됐어요.
examples.en: This land was first settled a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 아직 개척되지 않은 분야에 도전해 보세요.
examples.en: Try taking on a field that has not been explored yet.

explain: 아무도 가지 않은 땅이나 분야가 처음으로 열릴 때 써요. 사람이 열면 '개척하다', 열린 결과를 말하면 '개척되다'예요. '시장이 개척되다', '길이 개척되다'처럼 비유로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when land or a field that nobody has entered before is opened up for the first time. When a person does the opening it is '개척하다'; when you describe the result it is '개척되다'. It is also widely used figuratively, as in '시장이 개척되다' (a market is opened up) and '길이 개척되다'.

examples.ko: 글을 보내기 전에 틀린 곳을 교정했어요.
examples.en: I corrected the mistakes before sending the text.
I started exercising to correct my posture.
Could you fix the typos for me?

examples.ko: 교정할 부분에 빨간 줄을 쳐 주세요.
examples.en: Please draw a red line under the parts to be corrected.

examples.ko: 치아를 교정하는 데 이 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Straightening my teeth took two years.
After proofreading the manuscript, I sent it to the publisher.

explain: 틀린 것을 바로잡을 때 써요. 글의 오타를 고치는 일(校正)과 치아나 자세를 바로잡는 일(矯正)이 소리는 같은 '교정'이에요. 학교 운동장을 뜻하는 '교정'(校庭)은 또 다른 말이에요. 일상에서 말이나 행동을 고쳐 줄 때는 '고쳐 주다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is used for putting something wrong right. Fixing typos in writing (校正) and straightening teeth or posture (矯正) are written with different Chinese characters but sound the same as '교정'. The '교정' that means a school yard (校庭) is yet another word. For correcting someone's words or behavior in daily talk, '고쳐 주다' is more natural.

examples.ko: 사건의 과정이 책에 자세히 서술되어 있어요.
examples.en: The course of the incident is described in detail in the book.
I was surprised that what was written differed from the facts.

examples.ko: 인물의 마음이 길게 서술되는 소설을 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like novels in which a character's feelings are described at length.
This part is described briefly.

examples.ko: 방법이 순서대로 서술되면 따라 하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: When the method is laid out in order, it is easy to follow.
I am more curious about the story that was not told.

explain: 글이나 책에서 어떤 내용이 차례대로 쓰여 있을 때 써요. 말로 하는 설명에는 잘 안 쓰고, 논문, 기사, 시험 문제에 많아요. '서술형 문제'는 짧은 답이 아니라 문장으로 길게 쓰는 문제예요.
explain_en: It is used when content is written out in order in a text or book. It is rarely used for spoken explanations and is common in papers, articles, and exam questions. A '서술형 문제' is a question where you write your answer in full sentences rather than giving a short answer.

examples.en: He served as minister twice.
This is a person who served as a professor and department chair.
The person who long served as chairman stepped down.
After holding a number of posts, he retired.

examples.ko: 시장을 역임할 때 도로를 많이 만들었어요.
examples.en: While serving as mayor, he built many roads.
I hear he has a lot of experience from having served as CEO.

explain: 회사나 정부에서 높은 직책을 차례로 맡았다는 뜻이라 소개 글이나 뉴스에서 써요. 지금 하는 일에는 쓰지 않고 이미 지난 경력에 써요. 일상 말로는 '~을 했어요', '~로 일했어요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means someone took on high positions one after another in a company or government, so it appears in profiles and the news. It is used for past career history, not for the job someone is doing now. In everyday speech people say '~을 했어요' or '~로 일했어요'.

examples.en: I am worried because my child is home alone.

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 염려되어서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I cannot sleep because I am anxious about the test result.
If something worries you, please tell me.
I was concerned about my health, but I did not go to the hospital.
If the road freezes, I'll be worried about accidents.
If you feel worried, call me anytime.

explain: '걱정되다'와 거의 같지만 더 점잖고 격식 있는 느낌이에요. 어른에게나 글에서 '염려 마세요', '염려해 주셔서 고맙습니다'처럼 자주 써요. 친구끼리는 보통 '걱정돼'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '걱정되다', but feels more polite and formal. You often use it with elders or in writing, as in '염려 마세요' (please don't worry). Among friends people usually just say '걱정돼'.

examples.en: My parents always worry about my health.
Don't worry too much. It will be fine.
I worried that he might come alone.
Thank you so much for being concerned about me.
The problems people are concerned about are similar.
Instead of worrying about the result, use that time to prepare.

explain: '걱정하다'가 일상 말이고 '염려하다'는 더 격식 있는 말이에요. 어른께는 '염려 마세요'라고 하면 정중해요. 걱정이 저절로 드는 건 '염려되다', 내가 걱정하는 건 '염려하다'예요.
explain_en: '걱정하다' is the everyday word and '염려하다' is the more formal one. Saying '염려 마세요' to an elder sounds respectful. '염려되다' is worry that comes over you, while '염려하다' is you doing the worrying.

examples.en: I changed careers from office worker to cook.

examples.ko: 교사에서 작가로 전직하는 사람이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more people are switching from teaching to writing.
After I changed careers, my salary dropped a little.

examples.ko: 다른 업계로 전직할 기회를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a chance to move to another industry.
To change careers, you need a new certificate.
My friend changed careers and now works as a designer.

explain: 다른 지역이나 지점으로 옮기는 건 '전근', 회사를 옮기는 건 '이직', 직업의 종류를 바꾸는 건 '전직'이에요. 일상에서는 '직업을 바꾸다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Moving to another region or branch is '전근', changing companies is '이직', and changing the type of work you do is '전직'. In daily speech people also say '직업을 바꾸다' (change jobs).

examples.en: A small tumor was found in the test.
The doctor performed surgery to remove the tumor.

examples.ko: 이 종양은 암이 아니라서 걱정 안 해도 돼요.
examples.en: This tumor is not cancer, so you do not need to worry.
The size of the tumor is gradually shrinking.
I was treated for a long time because of a tumor.

examples.ko: 종양에서 조직을 조금 떼어 내 검사해요.
examples.en: They take a small piece of tissue from the tumor and test it.

explain: 몸속 세포가 이상하게 자라서 생긴 덩어리예요. 암인 '악성 종양'과 암이 아닌 '양성 종양'으로 나눠요. '혹'은 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이고, 병원에서 '종양'이라고 하면 더 심각하게 들려요.
explain_en: It is a lump formed when cells in the body grow abnormally. Tumors are divided into '악성 종양' (malignant, which is cancer) and '양성 종양' (benign, not cancer). '혹' is the easier everyday word, and hearing '종양' at the hospital tends to sound more serious.

examples.en: They say love transcends age.
His songs are loved across the ages.
I want to build a friendship that goes beyond borders.

examples.ko: 이건 상식을 초월한 이야기라 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: This story defies common sense, so it is hard to believe.
I started out wanting to rise above competition.

examples.ko: 말이 안 통해도 감정은 언어를 초월해요.
examples.en: Even without a shared language, feelings go beyond words.

explain: 나이, 국경, 시대, 신분처럼 보통은 경계가 되는 것을 넘어선다는 뜻이에요. 그냥 '넘다'보다 높은 가치를 말할 때 써서 '시대를 초월한 명작'처럼 칭찬에 자주 보여요. 대개 '~을/를 초월하다' 모양으로 써요.
explain_en: It means rising above things that normally set limits, such as age, borders, era, or social status. Unlike plain '넘다', it is used for lofty ideas and often appears in praise like '시대를 초월한 명작' (a timeless masterpiece). It is usually used in the pattern '~을/를 초월하다'.

examples.en: The old painting was damaged by humidity.
Be careful so that the cultural property is not damaged.

examples.ko: 훼손된 책은 새 책으로 바꿔 드려요.
examples.en: We will exchange a damaged book for a new one.
Once your reputation is damaged, it is hard to recover.
The packaging was damaged, so I returned it.

examples.ko: 자연이 훼손될수록 동물들이 살 곳이 줄어요.
examples.en: The more nature is damaged, the less room animals have to live.

explain: 물건이나 건물이 망가질 때뿐 아니라 '명예', '이미지', '신뢰'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 가치가 나빠질 때도 써요. '망가지다'보다 딱딱해서 법, 뉴스, 안내문에 많아요. 능동은 '훼손하다'예요.
explain_en: It covers not only objects and buildings being ruined but also invisible things such as honor, image, and trust being harmed. It is stiffer than '망가지다', so it is common in law, news, and notices. The active form is '훼손하다'.
